Get started

Installation

One installation route: the curl installer for Linux x86_64.

Before you begin#

The curl installer is currently the only supported installation method, for Linux x86_64 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu). You need Ghostty, Bash, curl, tar and sha256sum. No Rust toolchain is needed.

macOS code remains experimental, but there is no supported installer for macOS or other Linux architectures at this time. Windows is unsupported. Live draft reload and restoration remain unverified; CLI and TUI previews are internal samples.

Install with curl#

Terminal
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GiovanniCaiazzo01/Ghostty-wall/main/scripts/install-release.sh | bash

The installer downloads the latest stable release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum and installs into ~/.local/bin by default. You can change the prefix with INSTALL_PREFIX. Initialization remains an explicit next step.

Check which installation runs#

Terminal
command -v ghostty-wall
ghostty-wall --version

The selected path should be ~/.local/bin/ghostty-wall, or the bin directory of your custom prefix. An older Cargo or manual installation, such as ~/.cargo/bin/ghostty-wall, can take precedence in PATH. The curl installer does not remove or upgrade copies in other directories.

If the version still looks old, check the new installation directly:

Terminal
~/.local/bin/ghostty-wall --version
~/.local/bin/ghostty-wall update --check

Adjust those paths for a custom prefix. Put the new bin directory before the old one in PATH. For Fish:

Fish
fish_add_path --move --prepend ~/.local/bin

For Bash or Zsh:

Bash / Zsh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
hash -r

The Bash/Zsh change applies to the current shell; add the PATH setting to your shell startup configuration to keep it in new terminals. Recheck the selected path before initializing or updating. Your Profiles and History are unaffected.

Initialize your installation#

Terminal
ghostty-wall init

Initialization creates the managed directory, installs the Ghostty integration hook, and adds a bundled welcome profile to fresh installations.

Preview the setup

Use ghostty-wall init --dry-run to inspect the changes before writing anything. Existing profiles are not overwritten.

Keep the program current#

Terminal
ghostty-wall update --check
ghostty-wall update

This explicit command updates the curl-managed installation, including custom prefixes. It updates the executable being invoked, not another copy on PATH, and never updates Ghostty itself. Check the selected path above if an older version still runs. --check fetches release metadata only: it does not install or change user data. Already-current versions are a no-op; nothing updates automatically at startup.

The updater uses the version-pinned official Linux x86_64 archive, SHA-256 verification, bounded archive/platform checks and executable-version verification. The executable and .ghostty-wall-release.sha256 are published with rollback protection.

Progress distinguishes checking, preparing, verifying and installing. Keep other installers idle. Writable installation directories with atomic-exchange support are required; missing tools, ambiguous/mismatched ownership, substituted paths and manual/unowned binaries are rejected without privilege escalation. Repair ownership using the original installer, not by deleting safeguards.

Preparation failures leave the installation untouched. Publication failures roll back binary and metadata; if rollback also fails, inspect the recovery paths in the error before retrying. This is not a crash-atomic multi-file transaction: forced termination or power loss may require recovery from .ghostty-wall-update-* files. Profiles, Sources, History, Environments, assets and integration are preserved. Restart Ghostty Wall after replacement; a running TUI retains its old version. See ghostty-wall update --help.
